newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late on weather, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained broadly lower late Monday in fairly active trade, still undermined by milder East Coast weather forecasts this week which softened the cash, market sources said.
At 1410 EDT, August tumbled 7.8 cents to $2.09 per million British thermal units, while September was 7.2 cents lower at $2.07. Other deferreds were down by one-half to 6.3 cents.

"There was a lot of hype last week (about the heat and the hurricane), but there's no major weather this week. I think we're right about where we should be now," said one Midwest trader, noting the cash and winter premiums to spot futures should limit further downside.

He also said record heat last week coupled with some late-week production cuts due to Hurricane Danny likely slowed injections, raising the possibility of another paltry inventory build when the AGA report is released Wednesday.
"People are expecting a pretty small stock build this week, so storage could be a slightly bullish factor," he said.

Chart traders said they expected a pullback after August failed last week to pierce key resistance in the $2.23 area despite storm hype and some record heat. They now pegged August support at $2.08 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was seen in the $2.22 area, with further resistance pegged at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.
The following pipelines reported production was fully or mostly restored over the weekend:
- Texas Eastern - 200 mmcfd (less than 100 still cut)
In addition Columbia, which reported 270 mmcfd cut last week, said it expects production to be fully restored later today.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices skidded almost a dime to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were off more than a nickel to the $2.05-2.06 area. New York city gate gas skidded 15 cents to about the $2.40 level.
NYMEX said 32,928 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
On the KCBT, August was still down 6.3 cents at $2.015, while deferreds were steady to 4.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.5 cents to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
